$description: Stack-agnostic construction rules. What a project inherits when it adopts the MPC system, independent of framework.

note.en: Four depths, near-black and cool. Depth is carried by lightness alone — the site has no elevation shadows.
Copper in its interface role: the accent a visitor can act on. Two near-identical values exist here for historical reasons — see the note on --primary.
Background/foreground pairs for secondary UI. Always used as a pair: a surface token without its -foreground partner is how contrast bugs start.
Each carries a fixed meaning. Reaching for one because it looks right is the misuse this group exists to prevent.
White at low alpha rather than a solid grey, so a hairline reads consistently on all four surface depths without a per-surface variant.

A deliberately tight radius scale for rectangles. The largest value is 10px: the visual language is drawn with rules and hairlines, and rounded corners work against it. A shape that is a circle by meaning stays a circle; see the circle rule under Patterns.
Self-hosted via @fontsource — there is no fonts.googleapis.com request. The fallbacks matter: they are what renders before the webfont resolves.

rule.en: Own the LocaleProvider, the Nav/Footer frame, and section order. A route file should render a shell and nothing else.
Rendered by every shell. Links come from one navigation registry, never from a local list.
One argument each, opened by a `.label-eyebrow`. Carry `py-24 lg:py-32` and a hairline, except where the rhythm exceptions rule says otherwise; do not set a custom container.
SVG and CSS only — no charting dependency. Must collapse to a readable static diagram under reduced motion.

Carries no information, so it may draw on canvas or WebGL. `aria-hidden`; the copy beside it reads on its own; colours come from tokens at runtime; it pauses off screen, draws one still frame under reduced motion, and draws nothing without WebGL while the layout holds.
Exactly one may be visible at a time, and each declares how it yields to the others.
Wrap content, never replace it. SSR emits the final state so nothing depends on client JS to become visible.
Author colour as a token, never as a literal — with one exception below.

why.en: The published brand kit is derived from `tokens/*.json`. A literal in a component is invisible to that pipeline and cannot be handed to a partner.

rule.en: The exception: the whitepaper viewer (`.wp-*`) fixes its colours on purpose.

why.en: It renders paper. A white A4 sheet that followed the dark theme would stop being a document.

rule.en: Every animated utility must have a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out, and SSR must render the final state.

why.en: Content that only appears after client JS is invisible to crawlers and to anyone with motion disabled. Reveal and CountUp both ship the finished value from the server.

rule.en: Section rhythm is fixed: `py-24 lg:py-32`, separated by a hairline.

why.en: The home page is one continuous argument. Varying the spacing per section reads as unrelated pages stacked together.

rule.en: Rhythm exceptions — the only places a section may leave `py-24 lg:py-32`: the home hero ends at `lg:pb-12`; logo strips (partners, backers) run `py-10 lg:py-12`; a page head runs `pt-16 pb-14 lg:pt-20 lg:pb-16` with no hairline; the first section after a page head opens at `pt-12`; rows inside a list carry row padding.

why.en: Each of these sits next to something that already supplies the gap — the next section, the page head, the list around it — or is a band rather than an argument. Anything else that departs from the rhythm is a defect, not a new exception.

rule.en: Content width is `max-w-7xl px-6 lg:px-10`. Nothing sets its own container; a documentation shell divides this one into rails and a column, under the width budget below.

why.en: A single measure is what makes the hairlines line up across sections that were written months apart.

rule.en: A documentation shell with side rails keeps the content edge and a reading column of at least 40rem, even with a classic scrollbar. Inside `max-w-7xl px-6 lg:px-10` that is a width budget with 1rem left for the scrollbar, counting the column's padding on both sides (`lg:px-8` = 4rem): at `lg` (59rem inside the container padding) the left rail plus that padding take at most 18rem; from `xl` up (75rem, the container's cap) both rails plus that padding take at most 34rem. A shell that fits: left rail `14rem` from `lg`, right "on this page" rail `15rem` from `xl`, column `lg:px-8` — 41rem of text at `lg` and 42rem from `xl` up, about 40rem and 41rem behind a 15px scrollbar.

why.en: With `17rem` and `15rem` rails and a `lg:px-8` column the text gets 38rem at `lg` and 39rem from `xl` up — narrower than a comfortable measure for long documents. Showing a rail at a later breakpoint does not help: `max-w-7xl` reaches its 80rem cap at 1280px, so `2xl` adds no width. Only narrower rails or less padding do. Breakpoints match the viewport including a classic scrollbar (about 15px) while the layout gets the width without it, hence the 1rem of headroom.

rule.en: The radius scale is for rectangles. A shape that is a circle by meaning — a status dot, an avatar, a radio button, a switch, a ring in a diagram — stays a circle, drawn with `rounded-full`; a rectangle never rounds past `--radius-xl`.

why.en: "Never use a larger value" keeps panels and buttons drawn with rules and hairlines. Applied to a dot it turns a status mark into a small square that no longer reads as one.

rule.en: Status colour is fixed by meaning: complete or confirmed → `--positive`; in progress or provisional → `--alert`; planned or designed → `--muted-foreground`; failed → `--destructive-text`. Copper, gold and steppe never carry a status. Every status also states its word — Completed, In progress, Planned — so colour is never the only channel; each of the four colours clears 4.5:1 on the background, so the word stays readable. The motion utilities follow the same map: `.node-pulse` marks the in-progress stage and takes `--alert`; `.live-dot` (`--positive`) means a system running now, such as a live feed, and is not a completion mark.

why.en: Copper is the colour a visitor can act on, gold marks a figure, and steppe is the green that is not a status. A status painted in any of them says something the token was never meant to say, and a reader comparing two screens gets two different readings of the same stage.

use.en: Display face plus the -0.02em tracking it is designed with. Use this, not `font-family` alone.
Mono face for data and labels.
The eyebrow label: 11px mono, 0.18em tracking, uppercase, copper. Every section opens with one.
Balanced line breaks for headlines. Not for paragraphs.
Top divider at --border. The standard way sections separate.
Static 80px measuring grid. Structural texture, not decoration.
Copper-to-gold gradient clipped to text. Static counterpart to .copper-shimmer.
Wide, low-opacity copper glow behind a focal element.
Scroll reveal. Pair with the Reveal component — the raw class stays invisible until .is-visible is added.
Applied by the Reveal observer. Never author this in JSX. Reduced-motion neutralises it through .reveal rather than by name.
The measuring grid, panning slowly. Backgrounds only.
Light travelling across a copper headline. One per page — it is the hero's device.
Drifting blurred colour field for ambient depth. Absolutely positioned, pointer-events: none.
Travelling dashes along an SVG path — flow direction in the pipeline diagram.
A particle riding an SVG path via offset-distance.
Sweep travelling across a horizontal rail.
Pulsing node in a diagram. Marks an active stage.
Expanding ring in --positive. Reserved for genuinely live state.
